districts.enrollment_note: District-authored wording available only through search excerpts of martinezusd.net/registration and martinezusd.net/18445_3 (TK & Kindergarten Information). The repeated term "resident school" is the basis for the address-based call; an actual boundary map was never rendered, so this is an inference from district vocabulary rather than a boundary page read end to end.

districts.tk_capacity_note: WIDELY AVAILABLE district-wide, but specific school not guaranteed — asked whether there is space, the district answers "Yes, for all students who are age eligible", while also stating "The district does not offer guaranteed placement in a specific school for TK" and no priority registration for TK
districts.enrollment_note: Residency in the MPCSD attendance boundaries is the gate (verify address via the School Locator before registering); families refer to the School Locator to identify their neighborhood school. Caveat on seats: "MPCSD does its best to place students at their neighborhood school; however, school assignment is based on space availability at the time registration is complete" — if the neighborhood school is full for a grade, students are assigned to one of the other elementary schools. So address determines the district and the default school, but not an ironclad seat at that campus.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and flagged as the most consequential unknown. mvschools.org dropped every connection (socket hang up) across 5 paths (/enrollment, /registration, /registration-and-school-placement, /116149_3, /domain/29, /Page/73) and also failed via direct curl. Search summaries of mvschools.org pages stated repeatedly that placement is NOT done by neighborhood school boundaries but district-wide, and that TK is a district-wide program placed by space available at any district school rather than by K-5 placement priorities. That would make Mill Valley a rare non-boundary district and would materially change a family's ranking — precisely why it must not be recorded from an unread snippet. Verify manually before relying on the default address-based assumption.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained. "All eligible TK students will be enrolled and assigned to a TK program within the district. Assignment may be at a different school than the student's school of residence." The district also notes that for 2027-2028 all TK classes will be consolidated at one centralized location (380 Nova Albion Way), so the home school is explicitly not guaranteed for TK.
districts.enrollment_note: "Attendance areas have been established for each school" and "Attendance areas are based on home address," with a District Boundaries Street Grid lookup. Overflow is possible district-wide: students may be assigned outside their attendance area for capacity or class-balance reasons, and when that happens those enrolling before March 15 go into a lottery for placement (siblings prioritized), with results by April 1.

Not established — musd.org was unreachable from this environment on every attempt (WebFetch socket hang up on www.musd.org, musd.org, /enrollment and deep pages; curl connection failure; browser-pane navigation denied). Search results referenced a resident-school boundary map and TK at all elementary sites, but no district page could actually be read, so both facts are left null rather than reported from a search snippet.

School's Boundary Information page states: "The Moraga School District has established neighborhood attendance areas for each of the district's schools. These attendance areas determine a student's home school when they first enroll in a school." An intradistrict open enrollment policy allows transfer requests (due July 1, ranked against 1-5 criteria set by the MSD Governing Board, BP 5116.1). TK capacity NOT established: the district's TK and Kindergarten Information page covers only age eligibility ("students who turn four years old on/before September 1st") and schedules — no waitlist, lottery, limited-seat, or all-schools-availability language was found.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained — TK is hosted at designated sites, not necessarily your home school: "Students attending TK are already enrolled for kindergarten at their school of residence, regardless of where they attend our TK program." TK transfers are capacity-gated: "We will only accept TK transfer requests for TK students with siblings at the requested school and only if there is capacity."
districts.enrollment_note: Enrollment page offers a "Find Your School" home-school locator ("Search for your home school"). TK/Kinder Roundup FAQ gives priority enrollment to families who enroll online before the roundup deadline and check in at their school of residence. Separate transfer page notes waitlists are worked through summer and the first 3 weeks of school.

Not established. mvla.net closed the connection ('socket hang up') on five fetch attempts (homepage with and without www, /enrollment, /Enrollment/index.html, /apps/pages/enrollment, /Departments/Student-Services/). A search surfaced only third-party attendance-zone maps for Mountain View HS and Los Altos HS, which were not opened and are not the district's own publication, so nothing is reported.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained — "TK locations are determined according to feeder pattern clusters," meaning TK is not hosted at every elementary school and a family's TK site may not be its home school.
districts.enrollment_note: "MDUSD assigns neighborhood elementary, middle, and high schools based on street address." School Site Locator is offered as "a general guide to school assignments based upon address... not a binding determination." Two exceptions to pure address assignment: some streets are flagged "Choice (High School)" (student may attend any MDUSD high school), and Sequoia Elementary/Sequoia Middle are district-wide schools open to any resident. No lottery or ranked application for standard enrollment.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained. The district TK page states: "If your resident school is at capacity for TK and your child is placed at another campus, your child will automatically be enrolled at your school of residence for kindergarten." TK seats at the home school can and do run out, with placement at another campus as the fallback.
districts.enrollment_note: Read on nvusd.org: "Any child whose family resides in NVUSD's boundaries is guaranteed access by the California constitution to a free public education in NVUSD", plus a "Find Your School" section and school locator in the navigation, and "resident school" / "school of residence" language on the TK page. Out-of-boundary families use interdistrict transfer, "processed as they are received".

districts.tk_capacity_note: Likely constrained, stated indirectly: the enrollment FAQ says "Kindergarten and transitional kindergarten availability is the hardest to predict," and a transfer applicant "would have to start the year in his/her home school until we are sure that space is available." This appears in the intra-district transfer context, not as a description of resident TK enrollment; no TK lottery or formal waitlist is described.
districts.enrollment_note: "Students in New Haven are assigned to a resident school determined by their home address," with an interactive map ("Click on the map to search for your address's school of residence"). Ten of twelve schools serve their neighborhoods; the two alternative-education schools use a separate application. Enrollment is centralized at the Union City Family Center.

districts.tk_capacity_note: CONSTRAINED for home-school placement — "The location of the Transitional Kindergarten class may not be at a student's home school"; no waitlist, lottery, or seat-count language found, and the district's TK site list was not published on the page
districts.enrollment_note: Assignment inferred from district-published artifacts read this task: a "Find Your School" locator (newark-unified.schoolexplorerapp.com) linked from the homepage, plus the TK page's use of "a student's home school", which presupposes address-assigned home schools. The registration-guidelines page covers documents and residency verification only and never states the assignment method explicitly — so this is slightly softer evidence than the districts quoted verbatim above. No choice-lottery language appears anywhere on the site.

NOT ESTABLISHED. nusd.org returned HTTP 403 on /enrollment, /enroll, /tkk-eligibility, the site root, and a registration news post. No district page was read. Search results quoted nusd.org text about priority enrollment giving 'the best chance for your student to attend their neighborhood school' and reducing 'the chance of being overflowed or reassigned to another school due to space limitations' — which would indicate address-based assignment with capacity-driven overflow — but this was not verified on a readable page.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained, and the tightest grade in the district. "The district has rapidly expanded full-day TK programs over the last three years, but we still operate only one TK class for every 2.5 kindergarten classes. As such, current demand for TK is outpacing available seats." Also: "TK spaces tend to be more limited than Kindergarten seats, and are not always able to accommodate all of the families residing in a neighborhood boundary."
districts.enrollment_note: Explicitly stated by the district: "OUSD is a choice district, with no automatic school assignment." Families rank up to six schools and are placed by lottery-plus-priority algorithm. Neighborhood residence is only a mid-tier priority, not a guarantee — asked "Are families guaranteed their neighborhood school?" the district answers "No." Note the enrollment guarantee covers K-12, not TK: "all K-12 students are guaranteed enrollment in OUSD."

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area — "If you are unsure which school is your school of residence, you can utilize our interactive attendance boundary map on our District website"; enrollment requires two proofs of residence
districts.tk_capacity_note: Widely available — "Transitional Kindergarten is available for all students who have turned 4 years of age by September 1, 2026"; TK enrollment is at the school of residence and no waitlist, lottery, or limited-seat language appears on the TK page
districts.enrollment_note: Online TK/K new-student enrollment for 2026-27 opens February 4, 2026. Boundary and transfer questions are handled on the district's Enrollment and Transfer page.

Attendance Area page states: "School attendance is generally based on a student's residence address," with an address checker for the Orinda Union School District attendance area. Residency Verification is a separate required step. TK capacity NOT established: the TK/Kindergarten Enrollment page covers only the enrollment window (2026-27 window opened December 8, 2025 at 9:00 am) and age eligibility, noting "Orinda USD strictly follows the California Education Code on age eligibility." No waitlist, lottery, limited-seat, or all-schools-availability language was found.

districts.assignment_system: choice lottery — entry-grade seats allocated by a district-wide TK/Kindergarten lottery; residency inside PSD boundaries is the eligibility gate, not a school guarantee
districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained — TK is offered at only 4 of the district's schools ("offered at Cabrillo, Ortega, Sunset Ridge and Vallemar Schools in fall 2026") and seats are allocated by lottery: "The 2026-2027 TK/Kindergarten Lottery was held on Friday, February 6, 2026."
districts.enrollment_note: District TK/K/Lottery page: families submit "Sibling/Priority lottery cards" (due Feb 2) and "Transitional Kindergarten and New Enrollment lottery cards" (due Feb 4); results posted at the District Office. Eligibility requires being "a Pacifica resident residing within PSD boundaries or a PSD employee." TK-8 district; no attendance-area or school-locator language found on the enrollment pages.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained — TK at only 7 of the district's elementary schools, cluster placement 'if space is available'
districts.enrollment_note: Assignment: 'Your school assignment is determined by your home address, known as your neighborhood school.' If the neighborhood school is full a student 'may be overflowed to another school in your cluster' and is automatically waitlisted for the neighborhood school. Optional Choice Programs exist at elementary and middle levels alongside the address assignment. TK: 'Transitional kindergarten does not follow the neighborhood school placement process.' TK classrooms exist at seven elementary schools only — Barron Park, Duveneck, El Carmelo, Fairmeadow, Greendell, Palo Verde, Walter Hays — and 'PAUSD will place TK students in the school that is in the same cluster as the student's neighborhood elementary school (if space is available),' with students moving to their actual neighborhood school for kindergarten. So a TK family should not expect a seat at their home school.

District defines "school of residence/neighborhood school" as "the school that you are zoned to based on your home address," and provides a PCS Elementary School Boundaries Map (TK-6) and a Street School Lookup (7-12). The Aeries online enrollment application doubles as an intradistrict transfer application and lets families "select two schools and rank them in your preferred order" — a choice layer on top of the address assignment, not a replacement for it. TK capacity was not addressed on the enrollment, find-your-school, or FAQ pages read (only the age cutoff: "must turn 4 on or before September 1"), so that field is null.

Read on petalumacityschools.org (Casa Grande High enrollment-process page): students must identify "your school of residence", and "if you are registering for a school outside of your school of residence, you must complete and return a transfer form" (Intra-district Transfer Form offered for 2025-26 and 2026-27). Feeder junior-high students are "automatically pre-enrolled". No lottery or ranked-preference language. TK not applicable — high school district (grades 9-12) — but no TK statement was read, so null.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area — home-school placement is space-conditional
districts.tk_capacity_note: Mixed: a TK seat in the district is guaranteed for eligible residents, but the specific site is not — "We make every effort to enroll students at their school of residence, however if classes at one site are full, students will be redirected to one of the other school sites." So: program access open, site placement constrained. No lottery or waitlist.
districts.enrollment_note: "Students are enrolled in their neighborhood school whenever possible, space allowing"; enrollment boundaries page and a "Find Your Piedmont School" tool. Caution: the TK guarantee sentence on the page is still written for the 2024-25 year (birthdates Sept 2, 2024 – June 2, 2025), so the page is not fully current even though enrollment for 2026-27 is described as opening January 14.

Explicit: "All students are assigned to a school site by their residence address", with a "Find My School" PowerSchool locator. General (not TK-specific) capacity caveat on the registration page: "Depending on space availability, your student may be overflowed to another school site." Because that sentence covers all students rather than TK, TK-specific capacity is left null.

districts.tk_capacity_note: CONSTRAINED — site-level TK/K lotteries are held when enrollment exceeds available space; overflowed students are placed at another PUSD school and kept on a waitlist
districts.enrollment_note: Both facts read directly on the district enrollment page. Assignment: 'Students are enrolled in a school-based on their address', with a 'School Locator' tool provided. TK capacity: 'TK/Kindergarten lotteries are held at schools when the number of students that enroll exceeds the available space at the school site'; 'If a school site does not have space remaining in that particular grade level, the student will be overflowed (placed) at one of our other PUSD schools'; and 'staff will keep your child on a waitlist and call you during the school year if space becomes available.' Note the address guarantees a district seat but not necessarily the home-school seat at TK/K. Enrollments after Feb 28 are handled first-come, first-served rather than by lottery.

Registration step 1 is an Address Verification form, after which "District staff will verify your address is in the PVSD attendance area" before releasing the registration portal link. There is no school choice to make within the district: all TK-3rd grade students attend Ormondale School and 4th-8th attend Corte Madera School. Read no statement about TK seat limits, waitlist, or lottery, so TK constraint is not established.

districts.assignment_system: choice lottery — address does not fix an elementary school: "Elementary students (grades TK-5) can choose from any of our three elementary schools" (all middle schoolers attend the single Ravenswood Middle School). Note: the page describes family choice but does not spell out a lottery mechanism or any attendance boundaries.
districts.enrollment_note: Registration page states "If your child turns 4 by September 1, 2026, they are eligible for free, full-day transitional kindergarten (TK)" but says nothing about capacity, waitlists, or how placement is resolved if a chosen school is oversubscribed. Registration office at 2160 Euclid Ave, open weekdays 8am-3pm.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area (with an optional "School of Choice" lottery layered on top for specialized/immersion programs only)
districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained. Enrollment page (which explicitly covers "new 2026-27 students entering TK and K-8 grades"): "If space is not available at the neighborhood school at the time the family is enrolling during the spring and summer, students are placed at a different school until space becomes available at their neighborhood school. Students are enrolled in the order in which they submit their application." School of Choice page adds: "If a student moves into the area after the open enrollment period and their neighborhood school is full, they will be placed at a school that has openings," and "seats are limited and families transferring from another neighborhood school may be placed on a waitlist."
districts.enrollment_note: "Find Your Neighborhood School" school locator: "This is how you will find the neighborhood school assigned to your home address. Simply enter your address to discover your child's assigned elementary or middle school." Address governs the default seat; the lottery applies only to non-neighborhood specialized programs. Students attend TK-2 (or TK-5) at their neighborhood school — Clifford, Garfield, Henry Ford, Hoover, Roosevelt, Roy Cloud, or Taft. School of Choice options include Mandarin Immersion and Parent Co-Op at Orion Alternative and Spanish Immersion at Adelante Selby; new families must first register and be confirmed at their assigned neighborhood school before a School of Choice application is processed. Neighborhood residents get priority, then remaining seats go to transfer requests "via a random lottery."

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area — effectively district-wide, since there is one school per grade span (Reed PreK-2, Bel Aire 3-5, Del Mar 6-8), so no intra-district school choice exists
districts.tk_capacity_note: No constraint found — no waitlist, lottery, or seat-limit language on the PreK/TK registration page or FAQ; eligibility is age ("turn 4 years old on or before September 1st") plus residency ("reside within the RUSD boundaries"), with online registration opening January 21, 2026. Read as open, but the district publishes no explicit capacity statement.
districts.enrollment_note: Verified as the Tiburon/Belvedere Marin district serving Belvedere, Tiburon, and part of east Corte Madera. District publishes an "RUSD District Boundary Map" and a "Corte Madera Detail Map"; registration requires checking your address against district boundaries. No address-lookup tool and no lottery or choice policy appears on the boundary or registration pages.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area — single-school district, so residence inside district boundaries is the whole test
districts.enrollment_note: Assignment: 'The Ross School District (Board Policy and Administrative Regulation 5111.1) requires all students to demonstrate proof of residence within the Ross School District boundaries.' The district profile describes 'a single-site public school district serving approximately 340 students in kindergarten through 8th grade' — one school, so there is no school-selection or lottery step; no lottery, ranking, or application-window language appears anywhere on the pages read. TK: not mentioned on the residency, registration, or district-profile pages. The profile's stated grade span is K-8, which hints the district may not run TK, but the district never says so directly, so TK capacity is left null rather than inferred.

"Your home address determines which elementary school your child will be assigned to." District publishes a street listing to identify the assigned school among Brookside, Hidden Valley, Manor, and Wade Thomas; "All middle school students who live within the Ross Valley School District join us at White Hill." No choice or lottery process appears on the boundaries page. The district TK page describes only curriculum and philosophy — no host sites, seat counts, waitlist, or lottery — so the TK field is null.

NOT ESTABLISHED — sthelenaunified.org and shps.sthelenaunified.org dropped every connection (socket hang up) across multiple paths, including the TK page and the enrollment/residency-verification page found via search. No district page was read; a search summary confirmed a TK page exists and gave only the TK age-eligibility window, which is not the discriminating fact. Both fields genuinely unknown.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Not TK-specific, but the district twice states enrollment is space-gated: "All students in the District are assigned to a school based on their address of residence, however, actual enrollment is based on space availability at the school site," and the locator gives only "a preliminary school assignment." No TK waitlist, TK lottery, or TK seat cap is stated, so TK capacity itself is not established.
districts.enrollment_note: Boundaries were redrawn from five areas to four, adopted January 11, 2023, effective 2023-24; district provides a School Locator, a boundary directory, and a final map. TK 2026-27 opens January 13, 2026 for children turning four by September 1, 2026. Site sits behind a JS bot challenge (plain fetches return only the challenge shell); content was read by rendering the page in a browser.

districts.tk_capacity_note: LIKELY CONSTRAINED — UNVERIFIED: search excerpts attributed to scsdk8.org state TK, K, 1st and 6th are "nearing enrollment limits" due to "high demand and limited capacity", placement "first-come, first-served", siblings placed first and others "assigned to a school based on space available". Treat as a lead, not a confirmed fact
districts.enrollment_note: District site scsdk8.org returned HTTP 403 on every fetch (root, TK page, over both https and http), so no district page could be read directly. The TK signal above comes only from search-result excerpts quoting that domain — flagged unverified. Assignment method left null because nothing read distinguished an attendance-area default from space-available placement.
districts.source: scsdk8.org (search excerpt only; district site blocked with 403 — not directly read)

districts.tk_capacity_note: CONSTRAINED — oversubscribed schools allocate limited TK openings by tiebreakers plus random numbers; families join waitlists after assignment
districts.enrollment_note: Both facts read directly on sfusd.edu. Assignment: 'After researching schools, families list their school choices in order of preference and submit an application'; 'If more students request a particular school than there are seats available, then the assignment process uses a series of priorities, called tiebreakers, and random numbers to assign students to the limited number of openings.' Address is only a fallback — unmatched students are 'assigned to a school with available seats closest to the student's home.' TK specifically: 'If there are more students applying than there are openings at a school, choice assignments will be made by looking to all the possible combinations of tiebreakers in the order outlined here,' with TK tiebreakers being sibling, equity, and prekindergarten. Note an elementary student-assignment policy change is phasing in for 2026-27.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Not TK-specific. The district-wide capacity rule covers every grade including TK: when "the neighborhood school may be at capacity for the enrolling grade level... the student will be overloaded to the nearest school with available space" and is "placed on a waitlist to return to the neighborhood school should space become available." Enrollment itself is open year-round TK-12. No TK-only waitlist or lottery stated.
districts.enrollment_note: "School assignment is based on the legal guardian's residential address within a designated school boundary, commonly referred to as the neighborhood school." The district publishes a School Locator to "view your default school assignment." Staying at an overload school instead of returning to the neighborhood school requires an Intradistrict Transfer.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area — the district's own enrollment portal runs a "Find my neighborhood school" tool: "Type in your address and select a grade to look up your neighborhood school and see the boundary or zone for your location" (grade bands include Elementary TK-5)
districts.enrollment_note: Read on sanleandro.schoolmint.net, SLUSD's own branded enrollment portal (it links back to the SLUSD website); slusd.us itself was unreachable from this environment (connection refused via WebFetch, curl, and browser pane), so no TK capacity page could be read and that field is left null.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area (elementary and middle; high school placement is by Small Learning Community preference, not address)
districts.tk_capacity_note: Widely available. District states it "is welcoming new students in its transitional kindergarten (TK) and kindergarten programs for the 2026-27 school year," describes TK as part of a statewide initiative "available to all," and notes "Families do not need to live in the San Lorenzo Unified School District to attend our schools." Enrollment is open with "Central Enrollment ... open through summer." No waitlist, TK lottery, or limited-seat language appears on the enrollment or TK pages.
districts.enrollment_note: New Student Enrollment page: "Go to SLzUSD School Boundary Locator to locate your school attendance area based on your home address," and "Note: High School placement is by Small Learning Community and not based on address" — SLC "placement will be determined by the Enrollment Office, pending available space." Out-of-district families need an approved Inter-District Transfer from their home district. TK eligibility: turn 4 by Sept. 1. Site sits behind bot protection; pages were read via browser after direct fetchers were blocked.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Not applicable — high school district (grades 9-12, "10 Schools | 6 Cities | 1 District"); no TK program mentioned.
districts.enrollment_note: District site routes families to "School Locator and Boundaries" to determine the assigned school; the only 8th-grade content is transition material for incoming 9th graders. No lottery or ranked-choice process surfaced.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained — TK at only 15 named schools (3 of them transfer-only); overflow placement to another school when the TK class is full
districts.enrollment_note: Assignment: registration is address-based — 'Students must be physically living with their parent/guardian within district boundaries at the time of registration' — with a School Locator tool and an intradistrict transfer process as the optional exception. Priority registration closes January 5; later registrations are processed after seats may already be filled, and 'if classes are already filled at the time of registration, the Enrollment Office will assign...students to a school that has space available.' TK: offered at Audubon, Baywood, Beach Park, Brewer Island, Cottage Grove, Fiesta Gardens (transfer only), Foster City Elementary, George Hall, Highlands, Laurel, Meadow Heights, North Shoreview Montessori (transfer only), Parkside Montessori (transfer only), San Mateo Park, and Sunnybrae — not every elementary school. 'If your school of assignment does not have a TK program, your child will be placed at a school that does for their TK year and then return to their school of assignment for Kindergarten,' and 'If the Transitional Kindergarten (TK) class is full at the time a new student registers, the new student will be temporarily placed at the next closest school with space in the TK class' — an overflow placement, not a formal waitlist or lottery.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Widely available — "Every SRCS elementary school will have at least one TK class next year, as well as Kindergarten classes." Note a timing condition: completed TK registration packets are due by an early-March deadline "to be considered for neighborhood school placement."
districts.enrollment_note: "Every effort is made to place students at their neighborhood school"; to attend a district school outside your attendance area a family files an intradistrict transfer by the March deadline. District publishes a "School Attendance Boundary Information" page and a Student Enrollment & Family Center. CAVEAT: srcs.org repeatedly dropped the connection (socket hang up) on four separate fetch attempts across the root and three deep links; this content came from search results quoting the district's own enrollment and TK/K enrollment pages. Slightly lower confidence than directly-fetched rows. Also note the deadline nuance — TK seats exist district-wide, but late registration risks placement away from the neighborhood school.
districts.source: srcs.org (via search-result content; site dropped every direct fetch)

districts.enrollment_note: NOT ESTABLISHED — srcs.org dropped every connection (socket hang up) across www/non-www and multiple paths, including the enrollment page and the school-attendance-boundary page. UNVERIFIED SIGNAL, do not treat as fact and worth checking first: a search-result summary attributed to srcs.org stated the San Rafael HIGH school district "operates as an open enrollment district, meaning any student living within San Rafael may choose to attend either San Rafael High School or Terra Linda High School", with interdistrict transfer required for out-of-city students. If accurate this would flip the answer away from address-based for the high school district specifically (the elementary district does appear to use attendance boundaries), so it should not be defaulted to attendance-area. TK is in any case not applicable to a high school district.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Space-conditional rather than open-ended: a priority enrollment window runs November 1–30, after which "applications will continue to be accepted after November 30 and throughout the year on a first-come, first-served basis, as space allows at your resident school." No TK-specific lottery or named waitlist on the page.
districts.enrollment_note: Enrollment page instructs families to "Find your resident school using our School Site Locator" (schoolsitelocator.com/apps/sanramon) and refers throughout to the "resident school"; intra- and inter-district transfers are separate programs. The TK page does not say whether TK runs at every elementary site.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area (with an optional open-enrollment lottery layered on top for transfers)
districts.tk_capacity_note: CONSTRAINED — "Students will be placed at one of the TK sites based on availability" (stated twice); TK runs at "most SCUSD elementary school sites", not all; and "Open Enrollment does not apply to Transitional Kindergarten students", so the K-12 choice route is unavailable for TK
districts.enrollment_note: Default placement is the residence-based home school — eligibility is defined by living "within the Santa Clara Unified School District residency boundaries" per Board Policy 5111.1, with a School Locator tool. Choice exists only as an add-on: families "first enroll at your home school and then apply for the open enrollment lottery" for other schools/programs, as space allows. Address therefore does determine a school; the lottery is optional and secondary. Note TK students get no transportation.

Santa Rosa Elementary (K-6) is administered as part of Santa Rosa City Schools, so srcschools.org is the correct publisher. Assignment: the district FAQ page carries a 'Find my school of residence' locator task, and district text describes residence-area priority for the neighborhood school with a street grid of addresses used to determine school of residence; a valid in-boundary address is required to use online enrollment. The only lottery referenced is for charter schools, not for regular elementary assignment. TK capacity: the kindergarten/TK registration page and the FAQ page carried no waitlist, lottery, seat-limit, or per-school TK availability language, so TK is left null.

Santa Rosa City Schools' Find My School page: "Use the webtool linked below to locate the school of attendance for your address. We do not provide location services for addresses that are not part of the attendance boundary of our high school district." The registration menu lists "Find my school of residence"; the only lottery referenced is for charter schools. Important caveat: this is the secondary district of the two that SRCS administers — its own page treats the high school district boundary as distinct from the elementary school district boundary, and directs out-of-boundary addresses to their separate elementary district. TK/K registration therefore runs through the paired elementary district, so there is no TK seat to compete for at this district; TK capacity is left null rather than guessed.

districts.assignment_system: choice lottery — address does NOT determine the elementary school: "Parents may therefore request the transitional kindergarten (TK) through fifth grade school within the district they wish their student to attend, provided the student resides within the boundaries of the District and space permits," and "Proximity to school is not a criteria in placement." "Occasionally, a 'lottery' is required when registration requests for a particular grade level at an elementary school site exceed the space available." (Middle school is single-site: all residents attend Redwood.)
districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained — placement is space-dependent: TK-eligible-birthday students "will be offered the TK option first and then, space permitting, we will open it up to families" with slightly older children, and elementary placement at an oversubscribed site goes to a lottery
districts.enrollment_note: Three elementary schools (Argonaut, Foothill, Saratoga) plus Redwood Middle. District runs an open-enrollment/request model rather than boundary assignment for TK-5.

NOT ESTABLISHED. districts.enrollment_note: Assignment: 'Once the process is completed in its entirety, your student will be assigned to a high school based on your home address.' The district publishes a Boundary Search tool (schfinder.com/SUHSD). Incoming 9th graders may request a different school through Open Enrollment Transfers, which uses a random drawing when seats are available at the requested school and closes February 1 — an opt-in transfer layered on address assignment, not a district-wide lottery. TK caveat: the district serves grades 9-12 and its enrollment pages address incoming 9th graders only; no TK program is referenced. TK is therefore irrelevant here rather than constrained or open.

districts.tk_capacity_note: CONSTRAINED — TK runs a lottery with a waitlist. Applications by the February 28 deadline "are entered into the March lottery"; later ones are "processed in the order received and assigned based on space availability"; and "Students will either be assigned a school or placed on a waitlist based on the lottery results." Students are placed at their "school of residence whenever possible," "Transfers are not available for TK," and "All TK placements are temporary; children will return to their home school for Kindergarten." Mitigating: "TK classrooms are located at all elementary schools."
districts.enrollment_note: Note the split: general K-12 assignment is boundary-based (address-entry school locator; "If your home is located near a school boundary, your assigned school may vary"), but TK alone is lottery-allocated. This is the one district of the twelve where a TK seat at a named school genuinely cannot be assumed from an address.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area (single-school district — one TK-8 school serves the whole district, so there is no inter-school assignment to win)
districts.enrollment_note: District operates a single school: "Sunol Glen Unified School District is a public district serving grades TK-8, located in Sunol, CA." The new-student enrollment page sets a priority hierarchy with "Sunol Residents" first, ahead of interdistrict transfer applicants — residency is the gate, and no lottery or ranking process appears. No TK capacity, waitlist, or seat-limit language was published on the enrollment page, so TK is left null.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area — residence determines district attendance; intra-district school boundaries not confirmed on the page read
districts.tk_capacity_note: Not applicable — district serves grades 9-12 only, so it offers no TK
districts.enrollment_note: Read on the district enrollment page: 'Students are required to attend school in the district where their parent or guardian resides, unless they obtain an approved Interdistrict Transfer', and the district serves high school grades 9-12. No lottery or ranked-choice process appeared. Caveat worth carrying: the quoted language establishes residence-based attendance at the DISTRICT level; the page did not spell out how a given address maps to one of the district's individual high schools, so the intra-district boundary detail is unverified. Because this is a 9-12 district, TK is structurally not offered — treat this row as no-TK rather than as a TK-availability data point, and pair the address with the feeder elementary district for any TK question.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Not TK-specific, and a seat in the district is guaranteed: "Resident registrations are always welcome and placement is always guaranteed at one of our Union School District schools." The home school is not guaranteed, however — "If a grade level is closed, you can still register, and placement at another District school will be offered." No TK waitlist or TK lottery stated.
districts.enrollment_note: Step 1 of enrollment is "Find your Attendance Area" using a SchoolFinder tool to identify the "neighborhood (home) school," and "All new students will register with their neighborhood (home) school." One wrinkle: since 2014 the board has run Dual Enrollment Zones — addresses in those zones may pick between two named sites, and the chosen one becomes the home school; if that site fills during registration the family is assigned to another site with space. Neighborhood children have priority at their neighborhood schools.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area — "All incoming students are assigned to their school of residence"; district provides a school locator tool and school boundary maps. A short list of schools/programs is boundary-exempt (Buckingham Charter, Ernest Kimme Charter, Sierra Vista K-8, Fairmont Elementary).
districts.tk_capacity_note: Widely available with a space caveat — "TK is offered at all elementary schools in the Vacaville Unified School District" (10 sites listed; Alamo is PM-class only and Fairmont is AM-class only). No waitlist or lottery, but "Students are placed in schools on a space-available basis. If your school of residence is full at the time you enroll your child, your child may be 'overflowed' to another school within the District" — an overflowed student is guaranteed a spot at the school of residence the following year.
districts.enrollment_note: TK/K online and in-person registration for 2026-27 began January 5, 2026. Intradistrict transfers (formerly "Open Enrollment") are approved subject to available space.

districts.assignment_system: address-based attendance area (with two district "Lottery Schools" as optional specialized alternatives)
districts.enrollment_note: Enroll at VCUSD page: "Find out which school will be automatically assigned to your student based on street address." Intradistrict transfers are defined as moving "to another VCUSD school other than the one assigned to their home address." The district separately lists "Lottery Schools — Explore VCUSD's two lottery schools which provide specialized learning environments," so the lottery is an opt-in alternative rather than the assignment mechanism. TK capacity NOT established: the district's Transitional Kindergarten and Kindergarten page describes TK only as "an optional, free program available to age-eligible children" — an availability statement, not a seat-capacity statement — and shows no waitlist, TK lottery, or limited-seat language. Context worth flagging for a family: the district site carries an active "School Closures" section with intradistrict transfer windows specifically "for families impacted by closure" (Feb. 2-27, 2026), so school assignments may be in flux.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Constrained — a TK seat somewhere is guaranteed, but not at the resident school
districts.enrollment_note: Assignment: families 'Find your Resident School' using an interactive SchoolSite Locator by entering an address, and 'STUDENT PLACEMENT IS ON A FIRST COME FIRST SERVE BASIS UPON SUBMITTING A COMPLETE REGISTRATION APPLICATION' — order of application, not lottery. Priority Transfers and Open Enrollment exist as optional exceptions. TK: 'By 2025-2026 school year, all elementary school sites in WCCUSD will offer TK,' and 'All students turning 4 by September 1, 2025 are guaranteed a space in the Transitional Kindergarten Program... Due to space constraints, space may not be available at a student's resident school,' in which case a neighboring school is assigned. Enrollment runs on a first-come, first-served priority window rather than a formal waitlist or lottery, so registering early is what protects the home-school seat.

districts.tk_capacity_note: Not applicable — this is a union HIGH school district serving grades 9-12 only (Analy High, Laguna High, and the Academy of Innovative Arts), so it does not serve TK at all. Grade span read from state/profile sources, not a district enrollment page.

districts.enrollment_note: District operates one K-8 school (plus preschool); the boundaries page asks "Wondering if your home or prospective home is within the Woodside School District boundaries?" and directs families to confirm the address with the office, with a boundary map PDF and a separate interdistrict-transfer path for outside families. Both the TK Information page and the TK FAQs were read in full: they cover age eligibility (born Sept 2, 2021 – Sept 1, 2022 for 2026-27), the half-day-to-full-day schedule, registration opening January 9, 2026, and tours — and say nothing about seat counts, class caps, waitlists, lotteries, or what happens if demand exceeds capacity. TK capacity therefore left null.
